clue.text: A request for dessert, but not in a mess

definitions.meaning: read literally, an order placed for a slice of apple pie
the idiom for something neat and perfectly arranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a pudding, but wants it served without any mess.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a literal reading: an order for apple pie. The second is the idiom 'in apple-pie order', meaning tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a British idiom for complete tidiness, and taken literally it is also a pudding order placed in a restaurant.

clue.text: A pencil is needed to portray a bird

indicators.note: to portray something is to depict it in a new form, so the letters of a pencil are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist needs only a pencil to sketch a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelican is a large water bird with a pouched bill.

definitions.meaning: circuits of a track, as a runner completes them
takes liquid up with the tongue, as a cat does

explanation.surface: Someone does the rounds, buying drinks for everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner completes circuits of a track, and a cat lapping milk is drinking with its tongue.

clue.text: With little cash about, reduce order

parts.note: P, for penny, is a small amount of British money
RE is Latin-derived for 'concerning' or about
to pare is to trim or cut down

explanation.surface: Short of money, a manager cuts back on what is ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the abbreviation for a penny, the smallest British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To order things is to put them in readiness, to arrange or make ready.

indicators.note: the word for followed goes around the letter for right

parts.note: something that ensued came after, so followed

explanation.surface: A player tracked an opponent down the right wing, as was justified.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean guaranteed or made certain.

clue.text: Almost but not quite willing to study

indicators.note: the word is not quite complete, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: someone ready to help is willing

explanation.surface: A student is nearly, though not fully, prepared to hit the books.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject, in British usage, is to study it at university.

parts.note: an ex is something former, no longer current
a glaring error is plain, obvious to all

explanation.surface: Someone must justify why a mistake is no longer so obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: To give an account of something is to make it clear or give its reasons.

clue.text: The pharmaceutical product of two different plants

parts.note: the gentian is a blue alpine flower
the violet is a small purple woodland flower

explanation.surface: A medicine is made by combining extracts of two separate plants.
explanation.walkthrough: The medicine is not actually made from either plant; it is a dye named after the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: This antiseptic purple dye has long been sold by chemists to treat skin infections.

clue.text: Some stars get not one call. It's very odd

indicators.note: something very odd is strange or out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as its letters

explanation.surface: Someone finds it very strange that nobody has phoned them.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram pool is all of 'not one call' plus 'It's', thirteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of stars forming a recognised pattern in the sky, such as Orion.

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of the word egg is E
clips means cuts or trims
another egg head, a second E

explanation.surface: One intellectual cuts down a rival to put them in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like an intellectual but splits as egg's head, E; 'another' asks for a second E.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse something is to cast it into shadow or outshine it.

clue.text: Clean and drive away to accommodate a member

indicators.note: the word for drive away holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: shoo is the call that scares off birds or pests
MP is short for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A host cleans up and shoos guests out to make room for a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash hair or a carpet with a cleansing liquid.

clue.text: Thanks the organisation for food in Mexico

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
CO is short for company, a business organisation

explanation.surface: A company is thanked for providing the meals on a trip to Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: A folded tortilla with a filling, a classic Mexican snack.

parts.note: to pad something out is to swell or bulk it up
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: The army chaplain is delighted to be among the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' looks like an exclamation of approval but is a verb. The 's in 'chaplain's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Military slang for an army or navy chaplain, from the Spanish for father.

definitions.meaning: reddish-brown horses with dark manes and tails
a laurel wreath given to a winner, in the old sense

explanation.surface: Racehorses are given as a prize to the winner.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown horses share a name with the laurel garland once crowned on champions.

definitions.meaning: sticking out above a surface, as a nail head might

explanation.surface: Someone is excellent and knows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A joiner calls a surface that protrudes this, and the word also means feeling pleased with oneself.

parts.note: off can mean away from, as in off the table
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A gift has arrived from the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a noun, a gift, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something is to hold it out for acceptance.

parts.note: a is the indefinite article in grammar

indicators.note: the letters of the word entire are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece completely changes the direction of things.
explanation.walkthrough: AINTREE is a racecourse near Liverpool, home of the Grand National steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: This venue is a famous British horse-racing track.

parts.note: de is the French word for of
a fence is a criminal who handles stolen goods

explanation.surface: A Paris wrongdoer offers justification for their acts.
explanation.definitionFit: A justification or argument made in support of something or someone.

parts.note: a vent is an opening that lets air or gas out
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Building a new canal demonstrates initiative.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a crossword favourite among British rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A risky business undertaking, a bold project.

clue.text: Having transport in rain-storm is bliss indeed

indicators.note: the vehicle sits within the rearranged letters
a storm whips things up, so the letters of the word rain are rearranged

parts.note: a van is a vehicle for transporting goods

explanation.surface: Having a car during a downpour is pure joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rain-storm' looks like one weather word, but 'storm' is the signal to rearrange the letters before it; the vehicle then goes inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism, the state of perfect peace and happiness.

parts.note: taken as its letters

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: grab means take or seize
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A rallying cry to prohibit something and take nothing in return.
explanation.definitionFit: An official ban on trade with another country.

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A designer creates a pattern to suit customers' fashion tastes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' looks like a noun but is the verb, signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-out sheet used to paint a pattern, or the pattern so produced.

parts.note: suggests the High Church tradition of ritual, but means a tall part of a church building

explanation.definitionFit: A tall tower topped by a spire rises above many parish churches.

definitions.meaning: naming aloud, as a caller at a bingo game does
a strong inner pull towards a vocation

explanation.surface: Declaring a powerful impulse.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocation is a strong inner pull, and a bingo caller is announcing numbers.

clue.text: A monster held in no great esteem

indicators.note: the letters are held within the run of words no great esteem

explanation.surface: A beast is not highly regarded.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eating giant of fairy tales.

parts.note: reads as something mostly falling, but the main is the sea, and its level fell as the tide went out

explanation.definitionFit: The tide flowed back out to sea, lowering the water.

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction to play quietly
a lot is a group or set of people

explanation.surface: A conspiracy hatched among a hushed gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret plan, as in a conspiracy.

definitions.meaning: idle or lounge about doing nothing
British slang from rhyming slang ... of bread, meaning head

explanation.surface: Someone lingers about the top of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use your loaf' is British rhyming slang: loaf of bread rhymes with head.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to loaf, and in British rhyming slang the bread word means the head.

definitions.meaning: the only one, as in a ... option leaves no choice

explanation.surface: A diner complains that the fish counter offers no selection.
explanation.definitionFit: The single available option leaves no alternative, and it is also a flatfish.

clue.text: Could be a rum one to charm!

indicators.note: suggests these letters could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange character might well be captivating.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour someone is to fill them with love, to captivate them.

clue.text: In favour of half-a-dozen, so make this a requirement

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone favours six items, so insists on it as a condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A condition attached to an agreement, a stipulation.

parts.note: reads as money minted in his reign, but William III ruled jointly with Mary II, so was only part of the monarchy

explanation.definitionFit: A gold coin worth ten shillings, and also a joint monarch who shares the crown.
